introduction_markdown: Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1½ hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question (Section II: answer ALL questions, choosing one question from each pair of alternatives). For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Figure 1 shows a network of three resistors connected to a battery of e.m.f., $28\,\mathrm{V}$.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

*Figure 1*

figures.legende: Figure 1: a 28 V battery in series with a 5 ohm resistor and with a parallel pair formed by a 6 ohm resistor and a 3 ohm resistor.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the total resistance of the circuit. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The $6\,\Omega$ and $3\,\Omega$ resistors are in parallel:

$\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1 + 2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $R_p = 2\,\Omega$.

This combination is in series with the $5\,\Omega$ resistor:

$R_{total} = 5 + 2 = 7\,\Omega$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the total current in the circuit. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Taking the internal resistance of the battery as negligible, $I = \dfrac{V}{R_{total}} = \dfrac{28}{7} = 4\,\mathrm{A}$.
